caption: What if you could actually catch a shooting star? You'd be holding a speck of dust. Most meteors come from particles about the size of a grain of sand, 1 mm or smaller. But they hit our atmosphere fast: Orionid meteors arrive at about 66 km per second, quick enough to cover Delhi to Mumbai in under 20 seconds. They start glowing roughly 75 to 120 km up and usually burn away before getting within 50 km of the ground, most in about a second. October's Orionids are crumbs from Halley's Comet, which swings past about every 76 years. Halley was last seen in 1986 and comes back in 2061. This year the Orionids peak around 21 to 22 October: look up after the Moon sets, in the dark hours before dawn, away from city lights. How old will YOU be in 2061? 👇
